## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the competitive game to offer an endless continuation option beyond the win threshold (producer Q4: “option to carry on in endless mode”), so we can keep building after someone wins.

## Context

Competitive mode's win condition is first-to-threshold (parent CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30, phase-machine sibling). The producer explicitly asked for an endless continuation beyond threshold. Planning deferred this to a separate top-level issue (not a child of the competitive epic) so the competitive epic stays engine-focused and endless mode can land independently. N-player-ready design (PlayerRecord[]) is already in scope for the competitive architecture.

## Scope

- Endless-mode trigger and state handling after the win threshold is first reached (continue playing beyond threshold; scoring/phase semantics while beyond threshold).
- How the UI/scene signals “winner declared but still playing” (if any UI is needed here; full competitive rendering is the separate CG-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K child).
- Whether endless mode needs its own Monte Carlo treatment or is validated by manual play.

## Out of scope

- Competitive state model / phase machine / income routing / AI / harness / rendering — those are CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 and its children.
- Denial reasoning (separate follow-up).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Endless mode wiring is defined via an explicit opt-in flag/config: what triggers continuation, what happens to win detection/score/endReason/gameResult when play continues beyond threshold.
- [ ] **AC2:** Deterministic behaviour — same seed + same actions produce the same endless-mode outcome.
- [ ] **AC3:** Competitive mode remains playable without engaging endless mode (players can stop at the threshold win; default behaviour unchanged).

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Endless-mode flag/state.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Win detection vs. continue-beyond-threshold semantics.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-endless.test.ts` — Dedicated endless-mode tests (threshold win vs. continuation).

## Related Work

- Producer Q4 (CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30): “when one player reaches a win condition with option to carry on in endless mode” — now tracked here.
- Parent competitive epic: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 (first-to-threshold is the win condition; this issue layers continuation beyond it).
- Competitive rendering child: CG-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K — visual winner/continuation affordance.
- Competitive state/phase siblings on CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30.

# Validate before/after and update documentation

**Work item:** AC5, AC7, AC8 — before/after behaviour, documentation, test suite.

**Parent:** MS-0MUVB2ZES005V83Y (AI should not use Community Favour as much)

## Summary

After implementing the new heuristic, run the canonical Monte Carlo profile to measure the **after** state. Compare before/after, verify the win-rate ladder holds, update all documentation, and confirm the full test suite passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Before/after comparison recorded.** On the canonical profile (200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max turns, greedy, Easy/Medium/Hard), per-difficulty `rep→coins` uses per run are **materially lower** than the baseline. The Medium reputation-collapse share of losses does not increase.
2. **Win-rate ladder preserved.** `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard` holds. Committed-baseline tolerances (`winRate ±0.25`, `coins ±30%`) hold per `monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts`. Any drift beyond tolerance is reported via the drift-report-then-ask workflow.
3. **Documentation updated.** `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` and Community Favour move-evaluation notes are updated to reflect the revised heuristic. Code comments updated. Any relevant README entries updated.
4. **Full test suite passes.** All project tests pass with the new changes.
5. **Before/after artefact created.** A `docs/main-street/` artefact records the before/after figures and commit SHAs.

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` — committed-baseline tolerances
- `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` — AI strategy documentation
- `docs/main-street/` — before/after evidence artefact

data.comment:
AC5/AC7/AC8 — before/after validated and documentation updated.

**Canonical profile** (200 seeds, prefix mc-balance, 60 max turns, greedy, Easy/Medium/Hard):

| Difficulty | rep→coins / run (AC1 baseline 60867eb → after 6171307) | rep→coins / run (isolated: R2 base 159afa7 pre-heuristic → after) | rep-collapse share of losses (baseline → after) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Easy | 3.73 → **1.42** | 4.59 → **1.42** | 52.4% → **0.0%** |
| Medium | 3.14 → **2.31** | 4.79 → **2.31** | 67.7% → **12.1%** |
| Hard | 2.19 → **1.91** | 3.85 → **1.91** | 42.9% → **9.8%** |

- **Win-rate ladder** Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard holds (after: 0.735 ≥ 0.670 ≥ 0.385).
- **Committed-baseline tolerances** (winRate ±0.25, coins ±30% vs the R2-updated baseline) hold on all difficulties.
- **Medium rep-collapse share does not increase** (falls).
- **G5 band** widened to the combined design (producer option 1): reputation collapse 0.05–0.40, bankruptcy 0.40–0.95.

**Artefacts/docs:** `docs/main-street/favour-ai-after.json`, `favour-ai-after.md`, `favour-ai-evidence.md`; `ai-strategy.md` (new Community Favour heuristic section), `balance-guardrail-recommendations.md`, `further-balancing-recommendations.md`.

Full unit suite green.
